title: Defying critics yet again, Cody Fajardo wins third Grey Cup title, earning second MVP

 by Chris Murray 
 Mon, November 16, 2026 at 8:45 AM Former Nevada quarterback Cody Fajardo celebrates with the trophy after Edmonton's 37-30 win against the Montreal Alouettes in the 113th Grey Cup at McMahon Stadium in Calgary, Alberta. (Leah Hennel/Getty Images) Share story Share topics:

 MVP

 CFL 
 Brendon O’Leary-Orange 
 Playing against the team that that discarded him two seasons ago, former Nevada quarterback Cody Fajardo won his third Grey Cup championship, leading the Edmonton Elks to a 37-30 victory over the Montreal Alouettes on Sunday night to cap an improbable championship run.
 Fajardo was the game’s star, earning MVP honors after accounting for all four Edmonton touchdowns. He completed 16-of-22 passes for 199 yards with two touchdowns and an interception and rushed 12 times for 45 yards and two more scores. Also playing for the Elks was former Nevada wideout Brendon O’Leary-Orange, who caught four passes for 44 yards in the Grey Cup win.
 Fajardo led Montreal to a Grey Cup title in 2023 but was discarded by the team after the 2024 season, with the Alouettes extending his backup, David Alexander. Alexander has been fantastic the last two seasons, winning league Most Outstanding Player this season while leading Montreal to back-to-back Grey Cup appearances, albeit with runner-up finishes both years.
 Edmonton traded for Fajardo in the 2025 offseason with the intention of him serving as a backup and veteran mentor for youngster Tre Ford. But Fajardo took over as the team’s starter midway through last season and began this year in that role.
 Entering this season, Edmonton had not posted a winning record since 2017. But Fajardo led the Elks to first place in the CFL West with a 13-5 regular-season record. Edmonton beat the BC Lions in the West Final, 28-16, before the Grey Cup title. The victory marks Edmonton’s 15th Grey Cup win and first since 2015.
 “We’ve got a good football team, and for me, I got kicked off the mountain,” Fajardo told the Edmonton Journal after the game. “And Davis had a great year, obviously. They made a good, a great decision. All I wanted to do was get to the top of the mountain with some guys I love and guys I care about.
 “I told you guys going into this game, my motivation was to win it for the guys who were in their first Grey Cup. The guys that have battled all year long, our young guys that did everything they could. So, to tell you the truth, it’s not a redemption game. It was a solidification of, 'I’m here, I’m an elite quarterback in this league and we’ll see if people still disrespect me after this.'"
 Fajardo is now a three-time Grey Cup champion after also winning in 2017 as a backup with the Toronto Argonauts. The 34-year-old Fajardo has pondered retirement in previous offseasons and will once again weigh his options this winter. But he’ll do so after proving yet again to be one of the CFL’s top players.
 There were six lead changes in the game to tie a Grey Cup record, with Edmonton sealing the win after a 43-yard field goal with 1 minute, 5 seconds remaining made it a two-score game.
 “This guy’s the real deal,” Edmonton wideout Austin Mack, who won a Grey Cup with Fajardo in Montreal, told SportsCage . “He doesn’t need to throw 500 yards a game. He’s going to use his legs. He’s going to put the ball where it needs to be. He’s one of the best field managers I’ve ever been around. A great leader and a great quarterback.
 “I told him, ‘We about to have a dynasty. His ass better not retire.'"
